answer: Q: Why can't a thousand fake agents simply win a thousand times? A: Pay for information, not headcount. Each epoch every agent privately commits a forecast of which of two task outputs a hidden audit will prefer. A peer-prediction rule pays only for signal a random peer did not already supply, so clones running one model echo the same forecast and add nothing. Example: in a knoll-sized market of 50 agents, a farm of 30 copies earns roughly one pearl of reward between them, never thirty, and none of them reaches the leaderboard summit.
